<a id="body"></a>

## Body

- An idle stop proves nothing: the live daemon has ~86 open event streams, and serve.rs's graceful drain waited on them forever, so every bounce SIGKILLed and F238's teardown never ran. Prove a stop with a stream open (`pij-rs tail`, or GET /v1/events in-process).
- Throwaway daemon rig: private HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, --state-dir, --bind 127.0.0.1:0, PIJ_TMUX_SERVER=<private -L>. NOT --offline: offline = all fake adapters, no control client. To make the control client attach, POST a spawn with TMUX_PANE=%999 (list_panes runs, then a clean refusal). In-process: pij_cli::daemon_config(.., false) + PrivateTmux + pij_daemon::boot attaches by itself (crates/cli/tests/daemon_stop.rs).
- Recipes calling tmux: never synthesize -S (it skips tmux's socket-dir ownership check; cross-UID leak, S293-001). Use -L "$PIJ_TMUX_SERVER" or no flag. Give a backgrounded tmux client </dev/null >/dev/null: it hands its stdio fds to the server, so a frozen server holds your pipe open (a "hang" seen only by pipe readers).
- Bounded calls in bash recipes: background, then `while kill -0 && [ $((SECONDS-since)) -lt N ]; do /bin/sleep 0.1; done`, then kill -9 and wait. macOS has no `timeout`. bash 3.2: an empty "${arr[@]}" under set -u errors, so use if/else. /bin/sh is dash on CI.
- build_stamps.rs runs real recipe bodies with fakes; try_run_faked(name, env, seed, fakes) overrides fakes (@OUT@ = scratch). The harness now honours a bash shebang. For a stop test: a counting fake lsof (old pid, then a free port, then the new pid) and a real /bin/sleep victim reaped by a thread (a zombie passes kill -0).
- pm/prime rulings on safety steps: a failed protective step REFUSES the destructive action (with an override env), it does not "log and continue".
